tier_reason: README table compares unbuffered reads against fread and memory mapping on a stated Ryzen 9 7950X and Samsung 9100 PRO; code in src/ is public, but compiler and flags are not stated, so not A; first-party, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Unbuffered auto threads 11.3-11.4 GB/s vs fread 4.2-5.0 GB/s (auto) and memory mapping 6.8-7.3 GB/s (auto); single thread: unbuffered 4.7-4.9 GB/s vs fread 4.4-6.3 GB/s (fread can win single-threaded) and memory mapping 1.2 GB/s
corrections.caveats: No license; compiler and flags not stated; Windows-only APIs; page-cache state between repetitions unspecified; 2 commits; single-threaded unbuffered is not faster than fread (4.7-4.9 vs 4.4-6.3 GB/s); the win comes from multi-threaded unbuffered reads. Technique harvested from a benchmark repo, not a library.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly. Repo is a 2-commit benchmark harness (both commits 2026-01-22), no LICENSE file, so reference only.

tier_reason: README 'Language & Framework Comparison' table gives FluxIO vs Go os.O_DIRECT vs Boost.Asio IOPS; only benchmark/bench_fluxio.cpp is in the repo (Go and Asio harnesses absent), no CPU model, so first-party C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Peak IOPS (4KiB O_DIRECT): sequential write 715,827.6 vs Go 239,383.5 and Boost.Asio 86,783.1 (2.99x, 8.25x); random write 542,998.1 vs 248,800.8 and 86,821.4 (2.18x, 6.25x); random read 434,377.9 vs 308,629.1 and 22,192.8 (1.41x, 19.57x); sequential read 278,054.8 vs Go 302,860.5 (0.92x) and Asio 43,625.2. QD128 random write with FileBlockManager 429,229.3 IOPS vs Go 29,074.7 and Asio 28,411.3 on unmanaged sparse files.
corrections.caveats: Baselines are Boost.Asio C++20 file I/O and Go, not POSIX pread/pwrite or plain liburing; Go and Asio benchmark sources are not in the repo; FluxIO uses ~200% CPU (SQPOLL kernel thread) vs ~100% for Go/Asio and the README says IOPS per core is roughly on par with Go; sequential read is slower than Go (0.92x); the QD128 sparse-write comparison pits FluxIO's preallocation against unpreallocated baselines. First-party, no CPU model. Very young repo (9 commits, 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-04).

notes: Numbers match README. MIT license file present; 6 stars; not a fork (WebFetch reported '1 fork', meaning forked by others). Last commit 2026-10-04 confirmed.

tier_reason: README hyperfine tables compare gdu with du -hs and ncdu; benchmark commands are public in the Makefile 'benchmark' target, but hardware is only '500 GB SSD' with no CPU model and Go build flags unstated, so first-party C.

corrections.hardware: 500 GB SSD; CPU model not stated (cpupower governor set to performance)
corrections.workload: Scan a 90G directory (100k directories, 400k files) with hyperfine, cold cache (drop_caches) and warm cache (5 warmups); commands in Makefile benchmark target
corrections.claimed_speedup: Cold cache gdu -npc 4.716s vs du -hs 30.608s (6.5x, derived from page data) and ncdu 33.163s; warm cache 466.1ms vs du 1255.2ms and ncdu 2222.4ms. diskus is faster in both (4.489s cold, 270.8ms warm), pdu faster on warm cache.
corrections.caveats: Go, not C++ (a tool, not a library); CPU not stated; first-party table; gdu loses to diskus (cold and warm) and to pdu on warm cache; database-backed modes are slower than du.
